agent.result_text:
The duplicate claims list is in, and the main "duplicate claims" test passes. Two of the four tests in the spec still fail under `bin/e2e`, because of a mistake in the spec itself, not the app.

**What I built:** one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/claims/dups.slot.tsx`. It adds a `dups-show` button to the sheet. Pressing it lists one `dup-line` per person, date and amount that has two or more claims, as `<name> <date> <amount> x<count>`. VOID and DELETED claims are left out. People come in list order, then lines sort by date, then by amount as a number (so 9.00 comes before 10.00). It works from the people and claims the screen already loads, so it needed no server or database change and writes no audit records. It updates when claims change, for example after a merge.

**Test results** (`PORT=3000 bin/e2e`):
- **Passed:** "duplicate claims" and "duplicate claims scenario 3".
- **Failed:** "scenario 1" (line 192) and "scenario 2" (line 762). Both expect the literal text `__SHEET__-p` in `sheet-parent`. That's a placeholder that was never filled in. The app shows the real sheet id plus `-p` (e.g. `smvl4dwtkol5p-p`), which is right. I can't edit the spec, and making the app print `__SHEET__` would be wrong.
- To check the rest of those two scenarios, I ran a temporary copy of the spec with the placeholder replaced by the real sheet id. All four tests passed, and I deleted the copy.

**Port problem:** your shell sets `PORT=3002`, but another process (not this app) is already using 3002. With that setting `bin/e2e` can't start the app, the tests talk to the other process, and all four fail within seconds. I didn't touch that process. Run the tests with `PORT=3000 bin/e2e`. I saved this as a memory note for future sessions.

The spec needs `"__SHEET__-p"` replaced with `` `${sheet}-p` `` at lines 192, 329 and 762 for all four tests to pass. That's for whoever owns the spec, since I'm not allowed to edit it.
